name: csv-delimiter-bytes
instr:
Please add multi-byte field delimiters to `csv` and `csv-core`, so callers can read and write separators such as `||` without preprocessing the data. Don't add new crates.

Add these builder methods, each returning `&mut Self`:
- `csv_core::ReaderBuilder::delimiter_bytes(&mut self, delimiter: &[u8]) -> &mut Self`
- `csv_core::WriterBuilder::delimiter_bytes(&mut self, delimiter: &[u8]) -> &mut Self`
- `csv::ReaderBuilder::delimiter_bytes(&mut self, delimiter: &[u8]) -> &mut Self`
- `csv::WriterBuilder::delimiter_bytes(&mut self, delimiter: &[u8]) -> &mut Self`

The slice is copied and must contain 1 to 4 bytes. `delimiter(b)` is equivalent to `delimiter_bytes(&[b])`, and the last delimiter setter wins. For multi-byte delimiters, building must panic if any byte conflicts with the final configuration's quote, active escape, comment or record terminator. The reader's escape is active when quoting is enabled; the writer's is active when double quoting is disabled. The reader's quote is active when quoting is enabled. CRLF excludes both CR and LF. Invalid lengths must panic, with no particular panic text required.

Outside quotes, split on leftmost non-overlapping occurrences, as `str::split` would, including self-overlapping sequences. An unmatched prefix is field content, also before a record terminator or EOF. This must work through both core read APIs, with either `nfa(true)` or the default, regardless of input chunk and output buffer sizes. Positions count every physical input
